openTransaction(name) - Open a new Undo/Redo transaction.
This function no long creates a new transaction, but calls FreeCAD.setActiveTransaction(name) instead, which will auto creates a transaction with the given name when any change happed in any opened document. If more than one document is changed, all newly created transactions will have the same internal ID and will be undo/redo together.

getTransactionLog(fromSeq=0, limit=0) -> list of dict
Transactions of this document's log (docs/TransactionLog.md), each a dict with seq, parent, id, kind, origin, name, time, script, inverts (the seq an undo or redo inverts, else 0), who wrote it (sec 30.6): session, author (the user's name) and author_kind ('local', 'verified', 'invited', 'declared', or 'fork' for the desktop user of another copy of the file whose rows were imported), and uid, what the row is known by in every copy of the file: its session's uuid, a colon, and its ordinal in that session. Empty when the log is off (preference Document/TransactionLog).

getTransactionSessions() -> list of dict
The sessions of this document's log (docs/TransactionLog.md sec 30.6), one per login of one user: {'id', 'user', 'kind', 'name', 'access', 'host', 'opened', 'closed'} -- 'user' the id of the user row, which every login of one person shares; 'closed' 0 while the session is open.

pushTransactionActor(kind, name, access='edit', login=0)
Act as someone else from here on in this thread, in every document (docs/TransactionLog.md sec 30.3 S.b): the rows of the transactions opened until popTransactionActor() name that user as their author. `kind` is 'verified', 'invited' or 'declared'; `login` tells one connection of the user from another, 0 for one session per user. What a served document's host does for each client; here for tests and scripts.

popTransactionActor() -> bool
End the last pushTransactionActor(). False when there was none.

transactionLogin(kind, name, access='edit', login=0) -> int
Record that a connection was admitted (docs/TransactionLog.md sec 30.6 U2): its session is opened and a `login` row, a record with no ops, is written. Returns the row's seq, 0 when the log is off.

transactionLogout(kind, name, login=0) -> bool
The connection left: its session is closed. No row is written.

getTransactionOps(seq) -> list of dict
The ops of one logged transaction: op, ckind, cid, cname, ctype, prop, ptype, meta, before, after, derived. An empty 'after' on a set op is a value not yet resolved (see resolveTransactionLog).

getTransactionValue(ref) -> (fragment, {name: bytes})
The XML fragment of a logged value and its attachments, or None.

getTransactionVersions() -> list of dict
The versions of this document's log (docs/TransactionLog.md sec 16.3), each a dict with num, uuid, branch, kind, name, seq, env, docxml, schema, created, and manifest: a list of (entry, hash).

snapshotTransactionLog() -> int
Take an unnamed version of the document as it stands into its transaction log (docs/TransactionLog.md sec 16.3): a save's serialisation with no archive written. Returns the version number, 0 if there is no log.

restoreTransactionVersion(num) -> bool
Restore the document to version `num` of its transaction log (docs/TransactionLog.md sec 24.5): one transaction, kind `restore`, makes the document what the version was, and is an undo step like any. The document is not reloaded; view providers are not restored. False if there is no log; raises if the version is missing.

openTransactionVersion(num, createView=True) -> Document
Open version `num` of this document's file as a document of its own (docs/TransactionLog.md sec 27.5, 27.7): on the file's one log, at that version, named after the file with `@vN`, read-only as a partial document is. A version open already is returned instead. Its first change puts it on a branch: the one whose tip the version is if no document holds it, else a new one, `BRANCH@vN`.

saveVersionAsFile() -> int
Save this version document over its file (docs/TransactionLog.md sec 27.16), which save() refuses: the document takes its branch if it has none, as its first change would, and the file is written from it and reopens on that branch. The document keeps its name. Returns the version the save became.

saveToLog(name='Saved to history') -> int
Save the document into its file's history only (docs/TransactionLog.md sec 27.22, 27.28): the log records a version, named so it is kept, and the file gets the new history -- but what the file opens as is not changed. Refused for a pinned version, a document not saved to a file, and a file that does not carry its history. Returns the version.

getTransactionCursor() -> dict or None
Where this document is on its file's log (docs/TransactionLog.md sec 27.7): branch (its id, 0 for none yet), head (the seq its next row follows), detached (a version document not yet changed), version (the version a detached one is at), and documents (the names of every document of the file). None if there is no log.

undoTransactionFromLog(seq) -> bool
Undo row `seq` of the transaction log though it is not the last step (docs/TransactionLog.md sec 24.4): a new transaction, itself an undo step, applies the row reversed. Refused -- False, with the conflicts reported -- when anything done since changed a property the row set, a created object is gone, or a removed object's name or id is taken. Derived values are not restored; their objects are touched for recompute. False if there is no log.

nameTransactionVersion(num, name) -> bool
Name version `num` of the transaction log (docs/TransactionLog.md sec 16.3): a named version is never evicted. An empty name makes it unnamed again. False if there is no log or no such version.

getTransactionBranches() -> list of dict
The branches of the transaction log (docs/TransactionLog.md sec 17, 26): id, name, from_version, from_seq, head, id_base, last_id, created, closed, and current -- whether the document is on it. Empty without a log.

createTransactionBranch(name, version=0, seq=0) -> int
Make branch `name` from version `version`, or else from log row `seq`, or else from the current head, and switch the document to it; the version it forks from is named if it was not. Returns the branch id, 0 without a log.

switchTransactionBranch(name) -> bool
Make the document the head of branch `name`, in place. Not an undo step: undo and redo become that branch's own steps since the document was opened. False without a log.

renameTransactionBranch(name, newName) -> bool
Rename a branch. False without a log; no such branch, or a new name that is empty or taken, raises.

trimTransactionBranch(name, version=0, bridge=True) -> int
Trim a branch (docs/TransactionLog.md sec 16.7): its rows up to `version`, else up to the version at its head, and its unnamed versions before it go, never a row another branch holds, a named version or one a branch forked from. The version kept is named. With `bridge`, where another branch shares the history, the rows from the newest shared one up to the kept version become one row of their net change instead, so a switch between the two still walks rows (sec 27.71). Returns the rows removed.

deleteTransactionBranch(name) -> int
Delete a branch that the document is not on (sec 16.7): the branch, the rows only it holds, its versions but those another branch forked from. Returns the rows removed.

compactFileState() -> dict
Compact the state the documents of this file share (docs/TransactionLog.md sec 27.47): the name and last geometry id of every object nothing refers to any more -- no document of the file holds it, no op of the log names it, no version has it -- are forgotten, so the name is free again, and the strings of the file's hasher nothing holds are dropped. The id counters stay. Returns {'names', 'geo_ids', 'strings'}: how many of each went.

squashTransactionVersions(from, to) -> int
Squash the rows between versions `from` and `to` (docs/TransactionLog.md sec 16.7) into one transaction of their net change, undone and replayed like any; unnamed versions between go. Raises when `from` is not behind `to`, or a branch forks, or a named version sits, between them. Returns the rows folded.

openTransactionBranch(name='', gui=True) -> Document
Make a branch at the head this document is on and open it in a second document of the file, this one staying where it is (docs/TransactionLog.md sec 30.3) -- `name`, or `<branch>~<n>`. The new branch names this one as its target; neither follows the other, and one is merged into the other with mergeTransactionBranch(). Raises when the name is taken.

getTransactionBranchState() -> dict
Where the branch this document is on stands against the branch it was made from (docs/TransactionLog.md sec 30.3): {'branch', 'target', 'ahead', 'behind'} -- the operations here its target does not hold, and those of its target not held here. 'target' is empty for a branch with none.

previewTransactionMerge(branch, version=0) -> dict
What merging `branch` into the branch this document is on would do (docs/TransactionLog.md sec 28), read only: {'branch', 'ours', 'theirs', 'base', 'fast_forward', 'conflicts', 'changes'}. `base` is the newest log row both histories hold. Each change is {'kind', 'op', 'key', 'ckind', 'cid', 'object', 'prop', 'type', 'base', 'ours', 'theirs', 'note', 'derived'}; kind is 'take' (ours has not changed it), 'same', 'conflict' (a side must be picked, by `key`), 'view' (a view-provider conflict, ours kept unless picked) or 'derived' (not merged, recomputed). With `version`, the branch is merged up to that version of it. Raises when there is no such branch or the two share no history in the log.

mergeTransactionBranch(branch, picks={}, fallback='', version=0) -> dict
Merge `branch` into the branch this document is on (docs/TransactionLog.md sec 28): one transaction of kind 'merge', undone like any. `picks` maps a conflict's key to 'ours' or 'theirs'; `fallback` is the side of every conflict not picked. Returns {'seq', 'unresolved', 'failed', 'preview'}: a conflict with no side refuses the merge -- 'seq' is 0, nothing moved, and 'unresolved' lists them. 'failed' names the objects whose recompute failed on the merged state. The other branch is left as it is.

getTransactionForkBranches(path) -> list of dict The branches of the copy of this document's file at `path` (docs/TransactionLog.md sec 30.13, 30.14), as importTransactionFork() can take them: 'name', 'current' (the branch the copy's file reopens on, which an import takes when none is named), 'closed', 'base' (the row of this file's log the branch parts from, 0 when the two share no history) and 'ahead' (the operations it has made since). A file that carries no history offers one thing, itself, under an empty name (sec 30.19): 'base' the row of the save its Version names. 'independent' says the entry shares no history with this file and is offered all the same (sec 30.22): 'base' is 0, and what the file is now comes as a branch from nothing. Raises when the file cannot be read, or is this document's own.

importTransactionFork(path, branch='') -> dict Bring a branch of another copy of this document's file in as a branch of this file's log (docs/TransactionLog.md sec 30.13, 30.14). The copy's rows after the newest row both files hold are replayed in a document of their own, each committed here under the author and the identity it had; objects the copy made come under new ids, and under new names where theirs are taken; derived values are left out. `branch` names the copy's branch, the one its file reopens on when empty. The branch here is named after the file, and a second import of the same copy continues it. Nothing is merged: that is mergeTransactionBranch(). The dict has 'branch', 'from', 'base', 'rows', 'skipped', 'versions' (the copy's named versions that came as versions of the branch), 'extended', 'stopped_at' and 'reason' (a row that could not be applied ends the import, the rows before it kept; -1 when it is the file as found that could not come), 'renamed' and 'seq' (the import's record). A file that carries no history comes as one row, the difference between the file and the state at the save its Version names (sec 30.19); one whose history is there but is not its tip comes as what the history holds, that one row, then what it has done since. A file that shares no history with this one -- no row, no save of this log named -- comes too (sec 30.22): as one row on a branch from nothing, 'independent' true, which mergeTransactionBranch() merges by what the two documents hold. Raises when the file cannot be read, or a branch asked for by name is not there or shares no history.
